title: Parking Lot System
description: Design a parking lot that supports multiple vehicle types (motorcycle, car, bus) and multiple spot sizes. The system should assign an available spot on entry and free it on exit, and compute a parking fee.
requirements: Support at least 3 vehicle types with different size requirements
Assign the most appropriate available spot on vehicle entry
Release the spot and compute a fee when the vehicle exits
Handle the case where the lot is full
Design should not require rewriting core classes if a new vehicle type is added
constraints: Assume payment happens on exit only

title: Elevator Control System
description: Design the control system for a bank of elevators in a building. The system should accept hall calls (up/down) and cabin calls (floor selection) and dispatch elevators efficiently.
requirements: Support multiple elevators operating independently
Handle both external hall requests and internal floor requests
Pick a reasonable elevator to dispatch for a new request
Model elevator direction and door state explicitly
Design should allow a different dispatch/scheduling strategy to be swapped in later
constraints: No need to simulate real time precisely

title: Vending Machine
description: Design a vending machine that accepts coins/cash, lets a user select a product, dispenses it if funds and stock are sufficient, and returns change.
requirements: Model the machine's states explicitly (idle, has money, dispensing, out of stock, etc.)
Handle insufficient funds and insufficient stock as explicit cases
Support returning change and cancelling a transaction
Track inventory per product slot
Design should make it easy to add a new payment method (e.g. card) later
constraints: Assume exact set of coin denominations is fixed

title: API Rate Limiter
description: Design an in-process rate limiter that can be attached to an API to limit how many requests a client can make in a given time window.
requirements: Support per-client limits (e.g. by API key or user id)
Support at least one rate-limiting algorithm explicitly (e.g. token bucket, sliding window)
Make it possible to plug in a different algorithm without changing calling code
Handle concurrent requests from the same client safely
Explain what happens when a client exceeds their limit
constraints: Single process, in-memory state is acceptable
No need to design a distributed rate limiter

title: Expense Splitting App (Splitwise-lite)
description: Design the core domain for an app where a group of users can log shared expenses and split them (equally, by exact amounts, or by percentage), and see who owes whom.
requirements: Support at least equal and exact-amount splits, modeled so a new split type can be added later
Track balances between every pair of users in a group
Support simplifying/settling a debt between two users
Handle an expense involving users not all in the same group cleanly
Explain how you'd avoid floating point rounding issues in balances
constraints: No need to build the notification/payment integration
